PM1:✱2·33.source: PM volume I, first edition, p. 110
PM1:✱2·33.printed: p ∨ q ∨ r .=. (p ∨ q) ∨ r Df
PM1:✱2·33.note: Not an Aristotle theorem; audit the conflict with Lean's current right-associative disjunction notation before integration.

PM1:✱3·01.source: PM volume I, first edition, p. 114
PM1:✱3·01.note: Logical product is an abbreviation over primitive negation and disjunction, never Lean And.

PM1:✱3·02.source: PM volume I, first edition, p. 114
PM1:✱3·02.printed: p ⊃ q ⊃ r .=. p ⊃ q · q ⊃ r Df
PM1:✱3·02.note: This surface chain abbreviates the logical product of two implications; it is not right-associated implication.

PM1:✱3·03.source: PM volume I, first edition, pp. 114 and 116
PM1:✱3·03.printed: Given asserted φp and ψp of the same elementary real-variable type, assert φp · ψp
PM1:✱3·03.note: Must be a theorem of Derivation, never an axiom. The printed proof's circular citation is preserved and linked to uncertain apparatus APP-PM1-3.03-CIRCULAR-001; conjectural correction ✱3·01.

PM1:✱4·01.source: PM volume I, first edition, pp. 120 and 122
PM1:✱4·01.printed: p ≡ q .=. p ⊃ q . q ⊃ p Df
PM1:✱4·01.note: Equivalence is an Elementary abbreviation for the logical product of the two implications, never Lean Iff, equality, or an asserted proposition. Wikisource leaf 142 drops '. q' in the first occurrence; digital witness only.

PM1:✱4·02.source: PM volume I, first edition, p. 122
PM1:✱4·02.printed: p ≡ q ≡ r .=. p ≡ q . q ≡ r Df
PM1:✱4·02.note: This surface chain abbreviates the logical product of two equivalences; it is not infix associativity and not an asserted proposition.

PM1:✱4·34.source: PM volume I, first edition, p. 124
PM1:✱4·34.note: The unbracketed product chain is explicitly left-associated. It is a notation definition, never an asserted proposition or a theorem.

PM1:✱4·87.source: PM volume I, first edition, p. 127
PM1:✱4·87.note: By ✱4·02 and ✱4·34, read as the left-associated product ((A≡B)·(B≡C))·(C≡D), never as nested equivalence or Lean Iff.
